title: Stewardship Bridge Transition: Cache TTL Drift & Embedding Endpoint Degradation — 2026-12-05
body:
Summary:
We observed a progressive degradation in the embeddings ingestion and query endpoint from 01:10–03:45 UTC on 2026-12-05. Root cause at handoff: cache TTL metadata drift in the prefix cache layer plus delayed indexer batches causing increased cold-path queries that hit slower quantized backends. Customer-visible: increased 95th/99th latency for embedding queries and intermittent 503s for small fraction (~0.6%) of requests. No data loss, but elevated error budget burn for hosted-api tier during the window.

What I (Priya) saw during the shift:
- 00:58 UTC: Pager alert (latency-embed-95) triggered when 95th percentile > 450ms for the embeddings route for 3 consecutive minutes.
- 01:05 UTC: Dashboards show rising origin misses on prefix cache: miss rate jumped from 1.2% -> 18% in 10 minutes.
- 01:10 UTC: Spike in indexer lag on the async ingestion queue (kafka-partition-embeddings) with unprocessed backlog ~72k events.
- 01:20 UTC: Small burst of 503s reported by synthetic probes; correlates with autoscaler thrash on quantized-backend pod group.
- 02:00 UTC: Attempted mitigation: scaled indexer consumer + increased consumer parallelism (k8s deployment patch). Backlog decreased but not back to normal.
- 02:40 UTC: Discovered TTL override job (cron-cache-ttl-override) ran with stale feature flag set (feature.disable-dynamic-ttl = true) at 00:30 UTC — this caused many prefixes to be stamped with a large TTL and then subsequently marked expired by downstream consistency check, creating a churn of cache invalidations.
- 03:10 UTC: Hotfix applied: revert cron job config, reapply feature flag default, triggered controlled rewarm of hot prefixes from snapshot.
- 03:45 UTC: Metrics largely returned to expected baseline. Remaining error rate ~0.1% and 95th latency ~210ms.

Immediate actions taken (timeline + commands):
- 01:15 UTC: kubectl scale deployment/indexer-consumers --replicas=12 (from 4).
- 01:18 UTC: alerted infra-oncall (Liam) in #sre-bridge; started parallel investigation into cache telemetry.
- 01:55 UTC: grep logs for cron-cache-ttl-override in cluster-ops; found run at 00:30 UTC. Ticket created: JIRA-INFR-1193 (investigate TTL overrides).
- 02:05 UTC: Increased backpressure on write path (temporary throttling rule) to limit new indexer backlog growth.
- 03:12 UTC: rollout revert of cron job config: kubectl set env deployment/cache-cron CRON_TTL_OVERRIDE="" --record.
- 03:20 UTC: warming script run: /ops/scripts/rewarm-prefixes --list hot-prefixes-2026-12-05.csv (ran as dry-run first then actual).

Impact assessment (customer-facing summary):
- Window: ~00:58–03:45 UTC (approx 2h 47m)
- Symptoms: Elevated 95th/99th latency for embeddings endpoint, intermittent 503s affecting ~0.6% of traffic at peak.
- Scope: Hosted API users primarily; Dedicated customers routed to separate route saw negligible impact.
- Data integrity: No ingestion loss; indexer backlog processed successfully after scale and throttling.

Open action items (short-term):
1) Update embeddings endpoint runbook to include TTL-override cron sanity checks (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-12-07).
2) Add runbook step to detect sudden prefix-cache miss rate deltas >5% in 5m and auto-run limited rewarm (owner: Marco Rossi, due: 2026-12-09).
3) Create alert runbook snippet for indexer backlog >50k for >10m (owner: Priya Natarajan, due: 2026-12-06).
4) Postmortem draft (level-2) to be authored and linked to JIRA-INFR-1193 (owner: Priya Natarajan, due: 2026-12-10).
5) Add automated test to CI that validates cron-cache-ttl-override respects feature flags before rollout (owner: infra-eng, linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/592).

Notes to next shift (concise):
- Check indexer consumer lag (kafka consumer group: embeddings-indexers) and ensure lag <10k.
- Verify cache miss rate steady <2% over 10m. Dashboards: SRE > Observability > Embeddings > Cache Health.
- Confirm the cron-cache-ttl-override variable remains empty in staging and prod: kubectl get deploy cache-cron -o yaml | grep CRON_TTL_OVERRIDE.
- If miss rate spikes again, do NOT run a global purge; instead run targeted rewarm on top 500 prefixes (use ops script).

Runbook edits suggested (text to paste into Confluence):
- "When prefix cache miss rate rises >5% within 10 minutes and indexer backlog >20k: 1) scale indexer-consumers by x3; 2) apply temporary write throttling; 3) inspect cron-cache-ttl-override runs and feature flags; 4) perform targeted rewarm of hot prefixes; 5) monitor for 30m then escalate to Level-2 if >0.5% errors persist."

Follow-ups / Tickets created:
- JIRA-INFR-1193: Investigate TTL override cron and add pre-deploy guard (priority: P2).
- CON-8472: Update embedding endpoint runbook (child doc ID).
- GH-592: infra PR to add CI gate for cron env vars (link in linked_artifacts).

Unresolved questions / to decide in postmortem:
- Why did the TTL override cron run with feature.disable-dynamic-ttl=true? Is it a stale config in deployment pipeline or a manual rollback that never re-synced?
- Should we add a stronger post-deploy validation that compares runtime envs in prod vs. expected config (safety net)?

Misc notes / logs pointers (for triage):
- Kibana query used: loglevel:ERROR AND service:cache-cron AND message:ttl
- Metrics: prometheus/embeddings_cache_miss_rate, prometheus/embeddings_indexer_lag, prometheus/embeddings_requests_5xx
- Slack thread: #sre-bridge thread timestamp 1678329921 (see linked_artifacts).

Handoff checklist (tick when complete):
- [x] Incident context summarized above
- [x] Key tickets created and linked
- [x] Short-term mitigations implemented and verified
- [ ] Postmortem draft (assign and write)
- [ ] Runbook edits merged

Owner sign-off: Priya Natarajan (on-call) — leaving handoff to Liam Chen (infra oncall) at 09:00 PST / 17:00 UTC. Please pick up the postmortem draft and confirm runbook edits are scheduled.

Appendix (quick commands for next shift):
- Check consumer lag: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group embeddings-indexers
- Get current cron env: kubectl -n infra get deploy cache-cron -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env}'
- Rewarm dry-run: /ops/scripts/rewarm-prefixes --list hot-prefixes-2026-12-05.csv --dry-run

End of notes.
